questions.q: Why should every model in a comparison be scored on the same cross-validation folds?
options: It makes the models train faster
Fold-to-fold difficulty then affects all models equally, so differences reflect the models, not the split
It is required by scikit-learn
It guarantees the best model wins
questions.explain: Some folds are simply harder. If every model is scored on the same folds, that difficulty cancels in a paired comparison. Different folds per model add noise that can swamp a real difference.

questions.q: Model A beats Model B by an average of 0.004 AUC, winning 3 of 5 folds, and the fold-to-fold standard deviation of the difference is 0.011. What is the best conclusion?
options: A is clearly better
B is clearly better
The models are effectively tied on this data
Cross-validation failed and must be rerun on the test set
questions.explain: The mean difference is smaller than its own wobble, and the win count is mixed. Treat it as a tie and decide on cost, speed or simplicity.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a DummyClassifier baseline in the comparison table?
options: It shows what no skill looks like, so you can judge how much the real models add
It is the final model you deploy
It replaces cross-validation
It tunes the other models' hyperparameters
questions.explain: A baseline that predicts the class prior scores 0.5 AUC. Any real model must beat it by a meaningful margin to be worth using.

questions.q: Which scikit-learn tool repeats a whole k-fold cross-validation with different shuffles to give more paired scores?
options: GridSearchCV
cross_val_predict
train_test_split
RepeatedStratifiedKFold
questions.explain: RepeatedStratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=3) yields 15 train/validation splits, all reusable across models when you pass the same object.

questions.q: Two models tie on your chosen metric. What should you do?
options: Pick whichever scored higher by 0.001, since that is a win
Tune the test set on both and pick again
Report both as the final model
Decide on other factors such as speed, interpretability and ease of maintenance, then score the finalist on the test set once
questions.explain: A difference inside the noise is not a real advantage. Choose on practical criteria, refit the finalist on all training data, and use the test set a single time.
